questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large and neatly labelled diagram of the longitudinal section of the human eye. *(8 marks)*

How does the eye focus on:

(i) Far objects

(ii) Near objects? *(4, 4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Focusing on objects at different distances is called **accommodation**. It is done by changing the shape (curvature) of the **lens**, using the **ciliary muscles** and the **suspensory ligaments**, so that a sharp image falls on the retina.

(i) **Far objects**: the light rays from a distant object are almost parallel. The **ciliary muscles relax**, so the **suspensory ligaments become taut (pulled tight)** and pull the lens into a **thin, flatter shape**. The lens has a **long focal length** (less refractive power), and the rays are focused on the retina.

(ii) **Near objects**: the light rays from a near object are diverging. The **ciliary muscles contract**, which **slackens (loosens) the suspensory ligaments**, so the elastic lens becomes **thicker and more rounded (more convex)**. The lens has a **short focal length** (more refractive power), and the diverging rays are bent more so that they are focused on the retina.

questions.enonce_markdown: State four causes of deafness in humans. *(4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Causes of deafness (any four):

1. **Infections of the ear** (otitis media) or diseases such as meningitis, measles and mumps, which damage the middle or inner ear.
2. **Blockage of the ear canal by too much wax** or by foreign bodies.
3. **Damage to the ear drum (tympanic membrane)** by a sharp object, a blow, or a sudden loud explosion.
4. **Prolonged exposure to loud noise** (loud music, machines), which damages the sensory cells of the cochlea.
5. **Damage to the auditory nerve** or the **ossicles** (for example by injury), or **old age** (loss of sensitivity of the cochlea).
6. **Hereditary (genetic) defects**, or the use of certain drugs (for example overdose of some antibiotics, quinine).
